newsitem.title: ITALY: Too early to judge Italy crop damage - producers.
newsitem.headline: Too early to judge Italy crop damage - producers.

text.p: An abnormal combination of drought and frost affecting large areas of Italy for the past three months has hit fruit crops, but it is too soon to assess damage to cereals, an official of the Italian agricultural producers' association Confagricoltura said.
"It is too soon to put an estimate on the extent of crop damage," the official at the Rome-based body told Reuters. "But we can say that it is fruit that has been badly hit and not cereal crops.

"Cold and lack of rain can certainly cause problems for cereals and the yields could be down, but we won't see the effects until July," he said. Durum and soft wheat sowings in Italy have already taken place while maize sowings are just starting.

He said some figures already circulating about crop damage were unreliable, noting that in the extremely cold winter of 1995 crop damage was initially estimated at some three trillion lire when in reality damage turned out to be between 400 and 600 billion lire.
"We have experts out in the country and should be able to put a minimum valuation on damage in two weeks. In fact we should have some initial but reliable data as soon as next week," he said.
